**Keir Starmer**
The leader of the Labour Party since 2020, succeeding Jeremy Corbyn. He led the party to a landslide victory in the July 2024 general election and became Prime Minister, succeeding the Conservative Rishi Sunak.

**Opposition to the Conservatives**
Labour is the main center-left party in the United Kingdom and the traditional rival of the Conservative (Tory) Party. It served as the official opposition from 2010 until its 2024 election win, and this rivalry is the usual giveaway.

**Jeremy Corbyn and antisemitism**
Corbyn, Labour's left-wing leader from 2015 to 2020, was suspended in 2020 and then denied the party whip after downplaying a report from the Equality and Human Rights Commission that found the party had failed to deal with antisemitism. He was expelled in 2024 after announcing he would run as an independent in his Islington North seat, which he went on to win.

**2019 general election**
Under Corbyn, Labour suffered a landslide defeat to Boris Johnson's Conservatives in 2019, winning only 202 seats, its fewest since 1935. Many traditionally Labour seats in northern England, the so-called "Red Wall," flipped to the Conservatives.

**Shami Chakrabarti**
A human rights lawyer and former director of the group Liberty who led a 2016 inquiry into antisemitism and other forms of racism within Labour. Corbyn then nominated her for a peerage in the House of Lords, which critics saw as a reward and which undermined trust in the inquiry.

**Beergate**
A 2022 controversy over Keir Starmer and his deputy Angela Rayner being filmed with beer and a takeaway meal at a gathering in Durham during COVID-19 lockdown restrictions in 2021. Durham police investigated and found no rule had been broken. It was the Labour counterpart to the Conservatives' "Partygate" scandal.

**Sadiq Khan**
The Labour Mayor of London since 2016 and the first Muslim mayor of a major Western capital. During a 2019 feud on Twitter, Donald Trump called him a "stone cold loser."

**Rachel Reeves and the "non-dom" loophole**
Reeves, Labour's Shadow Chancellor who became Chancellor of the Exchequer in 2024, promoted a pledge to abolish "non-domicile" tax status, which let wealthy UK residents avoid UK tax on income earned abroad.

**Fatboy Slim violin lessons**
Keir Starmer has said in interviews that as a child he took violin lessons alongside Norman Cook, the musician later known as the DJ Fatboy Slim.

**October 2022 polling lead**
During the turmoil of Liz Truss's short premiership and the fallout from her mini-budget, polls in October 2022 showed Labour leading the Conservatives by around 30 points, a level not seen in decades.
